_note: One fixed synthetic learner per domain. Notes are written in the learner's own voice as rules of thumb, the form that produced the pilot's rule-echo case. No real exam content.

real.goal: I am preparing for a professional certification exam on building applications with large language model APIs.
notes: If an agent never needs a tool, remove the tool. Least privilege beats telling the model not to use it.
A tool that returns huge raw output should do the aggregation itself so the model only sees what it needs.
Cache reads never show up when the cached prefix is shorter than the minimum cacheable length.
Anything that changes early in the prompt breaks the cache for everything after it, so put stable content first.
Instructions inside retrieved content are data, not commands; enforce confirmation for risky actions outside the model.
An eval scored by the same model family that wrote the answers will flatter them; use an independent grader and a held-out set.

fictional.goal: I am preparing for the Tessellate 4 operator certification exam.
notes: Big ferries get split into shards and Tessellate never puts them back in order, so order-sensitive data must carry its own sequence numbers.
Eager ferries are faster but double the billing weight of the receiving lane.
Retries reuse the original inputs, so a retry never picks up fixed upstream data.
Pushing the retry limit above 5 turns off back-off and retries fire immediately.
Pinned lanes always run but only hold 3 tiles, and pins expire after 12 beats unless renewed.
Compacting the ledger saves storage but never lowers billing weight; merging half-full lanes does.
